svg.title: Causal broadcast: wait for the original before delivering the reply
svg.desc: Time proceeds downward. Vector components refer to A, B and C, in that order. A broadcasts m0 with dependency vector (0,0,0). B receives and delivers m0, then broadcasts its reply m1 with dependency vector (1,0,0). C is shown with separate causal-broadcast and application timelines. C receives m1 first. Since (1,0,0) is not componentwise less than or equal to C's delivered vector (0,0,0), C buffers m1. When m0 arrives, C delivers it, increments its A component to obtain (1,0,0), then delivers buffered m1 and increments its B component to obtain (1,1,0). Delivery events are spaced vertically for clarity and do not require another network arrival. Only relevant transmissions are drawn; self-deliveries and other broadcast recipients are omitted. Crossing paths are not events. These vectors count prior message deliveries, not arbitrary local events. Packet fields are sender, dependencies, message.
svg.metadata: Based on the user-supplied causal broadcast algorithm slide by Martin Kleppmann. LaTeX/TikZ, Latin Modern fonts, monochrome square boxes, and reference-matched arrowheads. All labels are vector outlines.
